sources: TUESDAY Oct 27 2026 RUN, pre-US-open (before 13:30 UTC), FOMC DECISION DAY MINUS ONE (decision Wed Oct 28, 2pm EDT). This run finally has MONDAY'S US CLOSES, so for the first time in several runs the equity-vol and credit tiles are not pure carries. HEADLINE: THE OIL PREMIUM IS DEFLATING AND NOTHING ELSE BROKE. Monday Oct 26 was a clean risk-ON session in the US: S&P 500 +0.70 pct to 7,676.77, Nasdaq +0.82 pct to 26,169.38, driven by Anthropic's public IPO filing reviving the AI trade plus falling oil. VIX closed 18.27, MINUS 6.1 pct from 19.45, the single biggest daily vol drop of the month. This morning Oct 27 the S&P future prints about 7,674 and the tape is quiet into the Fed. OIL - THE FADE STALLS BUT DOES NOT REVERSE. Brent 115.71 USD (TradingEconomics stats section; the quote widget shows 115.955 and the header a 0.12 pct change, dispersion about 25bp, does not change the read), roughly minus 0.1 pct on the day after Monday's 114.57 close (minus 1.8 pct) and Friday's 116.72 settle. WTI about 100.6-101.6. So Brent is BACK UP about 1 USD from the Monday low but still below the Friday settle: the escalation premium is leaking out slowly, not collapsing. Versus the Oct 20 run (110.85) Brent is still clearly UP week-on-week, trend stays up. The Houthi-claim / Saudi-interception cycle continues and STILL NOT ONE hit on oil infrastructure has been independently confirmed - NINTH CONSECUTIVE RUN OF THAT SAME QUALIFIER. Shipping-and-headline premium, not a barrel-count problem. METALS - GOLD LOSES 4,000 AGAIN, COPPER FIRM. Gold 3,999.24 USD/t.oz, minus 0.44 pct (summary text 4,000.72 minus 0.40 pct), giving back Monday's 4,025. Copper 6.53 USD/Lbs, plus 0.36 pct. Copper-gold 6.53/3999.24*1000 = 1.633, tile 1.61 to 1.63, up from 1.59 a week ago. Trend up. This is the cleanest pro-growth signal on the board. DOLLAR - TENTH RUN OF THE SAME ANOMALY. DXY 102.10, plus 0.08 pct (stats 102.088 plus 0.07 pct), after 101.96 Monday. Versus 101.93 on Oct 20 that is plus 0.17 pct, i.e. FLAT on the week. The dollar did not rally through the escalation, is not rallying through the de-escalation, and is not rallying into the Fed. Tile 101.70 to 102.10, trend flat. CREDIT - THE FRIDAY WIDE WAS NOT THE START OF SOMETHING, YET. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 HAS NOW POSTED Oct 23 at 3.38 pct, so the month wide is 3.40 (Oct 22) and Friday came in 2bp TIGHTER, not wider (3.27 Oct 21, 3.33 Oct 20, 3.29 Oct 19). Tile 340 to 338bp. Still about 15bp above the 323bp of a week ago, so the trend stays UP, but the one-day credit event did not extend. Oct 26 is not yet posted. CURVE - FLATTER, NOW CONFIRMED THROUGH MONDAY. T10Y2Y Oct 26 at 0.32 (0.31 Oct 23, 0.31 Oct 22, 0.32 Oct 21, 0.33 Oct 20). Down 4bp from the 0.36 of a week ago. Trend down. Monday's tape was actually a mild steepening at the long end (2Y 4.699 pct, 5Y 4.820 pct, 30Y 5.298 pct, 10Y held below 5.00 pct) but the 10s2s tile is still at the bottom of its October range. BREAKEVEN - THE BREAK HOLDS, FOURTH SESSION. FRED T5YIFR Oct 23 at 2.20 pct (2.19 Oct 22, 2.34 Oct 21, 2.31 Oct 20, 2.32 Oct 19); Oct 26 not yet posted. 13bp below the 2.33 of a week ago WITH Brent above 115. The market is still refusing to treat the oil shock as an inflation shock. Trend down. This is the most important single fact going into tomorrow's FOMC. VOL - EQUITY VOL BREAKS LOWER, BOND VOL BLIND. VIX 18.27 for the Oct 26 close (TradingEconomics shows 18.39 on its US market page, HDFC Sky 18.27 minus 6.1 pct; FRED VIXCLS last print is still Oct 23 at 19.45). Versus 18.07 on Oct 20 that is plus 1 pct, so the tile trend is FLAT even though the daily move was large. MOVE is CARRIED at 103.31 for Oct 23 - no free source served a fresh print this run (CNBC and MacroMicro both failed to load) - about 2 pct above the 101.1 of a week ago, trend flat. MACRO TILES - ONE REAL IMPROVEMENT, THE REST CARRIED. LEI y/y plus 1.2 pct September (index 99.6, six-month growth plus 0.6 pct) versus minus 0.7 pct a week ago: the single biggest week-on-week improvement on the board, trend up. Consumer sentiment 48.0, UMich October FINAL, versus 46.3 a week ago, trend up, but note 48.0 is still a five-month LOW in level terms. Jobless claims 194k week ending Oct 17, a three-month low, versus 199k a week ago, trend down; continuing claims still at a six-week high of about 1.73 million (little firing, visibly less hiring); next release Thursday Oct 29. ISM Manufacturing 54.5 September, next Nov 2. Sahm Rule 0.00 September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50. Building permits 1,400k SAAR September, next mid-November. NFCI minus 0.496 week ending Oct 16, next release TOMORROW Wed Oct 28 and it will be the first read containing both the Oct 22 and Oct 23 risk-off sessions. Global liquidity 1 (stable) on the Oct 21 Fed H.4.1, total assets 6,753,604 million USD, minus 2,035 million on the week, plus 2.5 pct on the year, no regime change at the ECB, PBOC or BOJ; next H.4.1 Thursday Oct 29. MONETARY PLUMBING - BLIND, TWELFTH RUN. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION at 0bp, not a measurement; every free source serves a SOFR level or an OIS rate but never the spread. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is likewise an ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp. Two assumed tiles plus one judgement tile out of eighteen, unchanged for a twelfth run. FED: decision Wednesday Oct 28 2pm EDT, target 3.75-4.00 pct, fed funds futures price about 90 pct probability of a HOLD (HDFC Sky, Oct 27). September PCE Thursday Oct 29. Midterms Nov 3. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy before this run (HEAD 2eef6b2, Oct 25 commit, Oct 26 run committed on top), this scheduled session remains the sole writer of data.json, the GitHub Action stays disabled since Oct 17, BDTI stays removed. .git now holds about 165 renamed lock files (HEAD.lock, HEAD.lock.*.bak, index.lock.stale.* and similar) that accumulate because this session cannot delete files in the folder - harmless so far but growing every run and it WILL eventually break a git operation; clearing it needs delete permission on the folder. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, TWELFTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in plain text in .git/config; fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Untracked junk still in the repo root: _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/. PICTURE: the risk scare of Oct 22-23 is being walked back, but only partly. Walked back: equity vol (VIX minus 6 pct), credit (HY 2bp tighter on Friday, not wider), oil (the premium is leaking), and the growth tiles actually IMPROVED (LEI y/y turned positive, claims at a three-month low, sentiment up, copper-gold up). NOT walked back: the curve is still 4bp flatter than a week ago and the 5y5y breakeven is still 13bp lower with Brent above 115. So the board now reads as a GROWTH-OK, INFLATION-FADING, COST-OF-CAPITAL-STILL-TIGHTER mix going into the Fed, with the dovish tail live and nothing in the hard data broken. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: the FOMC tomorrow Oct 28 and whether the statement acknowledges the oil shock as transitory (the breakeven says the market already has); the Oct 28 NFCI, first read containing both risk-off sessions; whether HY OAS keeps grinding back inside 338 when Oct 26 posts; September PCE Thursday Oct 29; whether the Brent fade extends toward the 108 bear case or the 120 bull case; whether any Saudi barrel or Yanbu hit is EVER confirmed; rotating the embedded PAT; clearing the 165 .git lock files.
